newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - EU launches detailed probe into Dutch toys deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - EU launches detailed probe into Dutch toys deal.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it would start an in-depth competition probe into the planned takeover of the Dutch unit of U.S. giant Toys 'R Us by Blokker Holding BV.

The European Union executive said Blokker had by far the largest market share as a toy retailer in the Netherlands and therefore held a "significant position as a retailer and as a purchaser of toys" in the country.

"In assessing the operation, the Commission in particular needs to examine the effect of the combination of the Toys 'R Us 'mega' stores with Blokker's familiarity with the Dutch retail market," the Commission said in a statement.
"The Commission now has a maximum of a further four months in which to complete its inquiries and take a final decision on the case," it added.
A Blokker spokesman declined to comment on the probe.
The deal was submitted for clearance by the Dutch authorities. The Commission would otherwise not have competence over the operation because it affects mainly the Netherlands.
It is the third time that the Commission has opened a second phase merger inquiry into a deal referred to it by a member state.
Toys 'R Us Netherlands is a wholly owned subsidiary of Toys 'R Us Inc of the United States, one of the world's biggest toy retailers.
It currently operates nine megastores in the Netherlands of which three would be closed if the operation was approved, the Commission said.
Blokker is a retail chain mainly active in household articles, toys and other products.
According to press reports last year, the Dutch government had expressed concerns about the impact of the Toys 'R Us takeover on the market for toy retailing.
On Wednesday, Dutch newsagency ANP reported that Blokker's market share in toys business in the Netherlands would increase to 51 percent from 44 percent if the deal was approved.
In 1995, Dutch authorities also asked to Commission to examine a joint venture in the television sector called the Holland Media Groep, which the EU's competition watchdog substantially modified.
In another case referred to the Commission by local authorities, the planned merger between Finnish retailers and wholesalers Kesko and Tuko was blocked by the Commission last year.
